interpretation.disclaimer: LLM-generated interpretation. Deterministic facts remain in the separate engineering report.

executive_synthesis.headline: The system recovered, but the replay task exposed a specification and routing gap.
executive_synthesis.summary: Rework was concentrated rather than systemic. The largest hotspot combined an unstated migration invariant, reactive skill use, and a late validator handoff. Human input was most valuable at the architecture boundary; routine performance recovery occurred without human intervention.

findings.title: Replay ordering was the dominant improvement target
findings.statement: Four loops and two agents concentrated on one task, while most phases and tasks completed with little or no rework.
findings.uncertainty: Task complexity is not normalized, so this is a hotspot finding rather than an agent-efficiency judgment.
findings.recommended_action: Make the migration-ordering invariant explicit before implementation and require a replay fixture in the task acceptance criteria.
findings.verification_plan: Compare loops and validation attempts on the next replay task using the new fixture.

findings.title: Validator involvement arrived after repeated integration failure
findings.statement: The handoff to Validator 02 occurred only in the fourth loop. Earlier validator review may reduce repeated migration-ordering failures.
counter_evidence: Earlier validator involvement could add overhead on routine tasks.
findings.uncertainty: The report does not contain a controlled comparison with early validator routing.
findings.recommended_action: Route a validator at plan approval for tasks touching replay ordering or migrations.
findings.verification_plan: Run the next two qualifying tasks with early validator review and compare rework events without using a quality score.

findings.title: Human judgment was valuable at the invariant boundary, not routine recovery
findings.statement: The replay task needed one human clarification about the migration invariant, while the stop-hook performance task recovered through agent work and validation without a human event.
findings.uncertainty: Only captured human events are classified; off-channel intervention would be unknown.
findings.recommended_action: Reserve human escalation for invariant, acceptance, permission, and architectural decisions; keep routine debug recovery agent-led.
findings.verification_plan: Track classification and unknown capture rate across the next ten recovery intervals.

findings.title: Rust debugging was used reactively after failures
findings.statement: The rust-debugging skill was invoked after replay failures rather than preloaded for the task. This suggests a routing or task-template opportunity.
counter_evidence: Preloading more skills may increase context and token use.
findings.uncertainty: Skill invocation is correlated with the task; the report cannot prove that preloading would prevent failure.
findings.recommended_action: Add a replay-task profile that preloads migration and debugging guidance only when task scope matches.
findings.verification_plan: A/B the profile on comparable replay fixtures and inspect loops, tokens, and validation outcomes.

findings.title: Final handoff understated the recovery path
findings.statement: Three recorded replay validation failures were absent from the final handoff. The system should require material failure and recovery disclosure at task completion.
findings.uncertainty: The handoff may have been intentionally concise, but the omitted failures were material to future maintenance.
findings.recommended_action: Add an automated completion note section listing failed validations, human interventions, superseded outputs, and unresolved risks.
findings.verification_plan: Completion gate rejects a handoff when material evidence categories are omitted.

findings.title: The migration assumption should become a system asset
findings.statement: The agent's explicit monotonic-migration assumption is reusable knowledge and should be promoted into the replay specification, a failing fixture, and the migration skill.
findings.uncertainty: The exact invariant should be confirmed against current migration semantics before promotion.
findings.recommended_action: Promote one observation into three synchronized assets: specification rule, regression test, and skill update.
findings.verification_plan: The next replay task must cite the rule and pass the new fixture before completion.

experiments.title: Replay ordering contract
experiments.red: Add a fixture that replays non-monotonic migration metadata and fails under the current ordering assumption.
experiments.green: Implement an explicit replay ordering contract and validator that passes the fixture.
experiments.optimize: Preload the migration skill and route a validator at plan approval only for matching tasks.

experiments.title: Evidence-complete handoff
experiments.red: Create a golden handoff that fails when material validation failures or human interventions are omitted.
experiments.green: Generate an evidence-backed completion summary from task facts.
experiments.optimize: Keep the summary concise while preserving links to full evidence.

experiments.title: Selective skill preload
experiments.red: Record the current reactive skill-use baseline on a replay fixture.
experiments.green: Add a task-profile rule that preloads migration/debugging skills for matching scope.
experiments.optimize: Remove unnecessary preload when the task classifier confidence is low.
